module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Feit-Thompson conjecture on primes

*Reference:* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feit%E2%80%93Thompson_conjecture)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace FeitThompsonPrimeConjecture

/--
There are no distinct primes $p$ and $q$ such that $\frac{q^p - 1}{q - 1}$ divides $\frac{p^q - 1}{p - 1}$
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem feit_thompson_primes (p q : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (hq : q.Prime) (h : p < q) :
    ¬ (q ^ p - 1) / (q - 1) ∣ (p ^ q - 1) / (p - 1) := by
  sorry

end FeitThompsonPrimeConjecture

reformulations.difference: Wikipedia forbids (p^q−1)/(p−1) dividing (q^p−1)/(q−1) for all distinct primes. Lean swaps the variable roles and restricts to p < q.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Write R(b,n)=(b^n−1)/(b−1). After swapping Wikipedia's variables, its statement is ¬R(q,p) ∣ R(p,q) for all distinct primes. The omitted case q < p holds automatically because 0 < R(p,q) < R(q,p). For q ≥ 3, monotonicity of log(x)/x on [e,∞) gives p^q ≤ q^p; the strictly smaller denominator q−1 then gives the strict quotient inequality. For q=2, it reduces to p+1 < 2^p−1 for p≥3. Thus the omitted ordering cannot contain a counterexample. The exact equivalence with the declaration's type was proved in /workspace/review/ordering.lean as Review.source_noexist_iff_declaration; its axioms contain no sorryAx.

sources_consulted: Checked-out Mathlib: Mathlib/Algebra/Ring/GeomSum.lean (natural-number geometric sums and exact divisibility).
review.notes: Checked the file's sole declaration. Primality excludes 0 and 1, so denominators are positive and natural subtraction does not truncate. Both natural-number divisions are exact geometric sums, verified in Lean. Tested the smallest permitted pair (2,3), both orderings, and all distinct prime pairs below 100. Also confirmed that the source's (17,3313) example has gcd 112643 but neither quotient divides the other: it disproves only the stronger coprimality claim, not the statement in this file. The research-open tag agrees with the cited source.
